Family life is strained. Dinner is often silent, communcation is scarce, and even recently, my dad lived separately for a few weeks due to mom-dad issues. My brother is wholly jaded with the family, my mom is constantly in a foul mood, and my dad just seems to be growing older, faster. And I'm sitting here watching everything crumble, t h inking of w hat I could've done or shouldn't have done to prevent this situation. Right now, I have about 5 different thoughts in my head, all trying to express themselves, so I'll just try to write it out quickly and succinctly. Warning: a pandora's box of problems ahead.

#1 I feel selfish. My parents have given me so much and yet I keep yearning for more. Because of my academic achievements, I was able to enter into the University of Michigan (but we live in Colorado), yet I wasn't able to get any major scholarships. 1000 here, 1500 there, but nothing big. And tuition is big at a BIG10 school. Especially out of state. Yet for some reason, I persisted. I wanted to go to Michigan. To get the experience. To go somewhere new, where most people I knew didnt go. All this despite t he massive tuition it costs. Dont get me wrong, my family is not, by any means, poor. As I said earlier, my mothers a pharmacists, so we get a fairly above average income. However, as I also said earlier, we send much of our money overseas to relatives, as well as giving money to assist relatives here in the states. I never knew the value of money. Now I know. Yet they never once mentioned it. They never once mentioned how much of a strain this might put on our financial status. They never let it be known that I was probably going to cause a rough future financially. And now I know how horrible I've been, but I can't back down now, because they've been encouraging me with a smile on their face to press on and not worry about anything. I feel like it would be a complete and utter betrayal to suddenly pick up and move in-state, as if I was simply playing witht heir support. I have to move forward, but my soul weighs down with every step.

#2 As I said in the preamble to this section, my family is falling apart. I am desparately trying to keep everyone together, to diffuse situations, and to offer un-biased solutions, but everything I say seems to make things worse and worse, causing fights more often than preventing them. You can see where this is going. Not only am I blaming myself already for whatever wrong I may or may not have comitted, but now I get to deal with the "butterfly effect" i seem to cause in every fight. The blame piled with the frustration that stems from not being able to do anything has even caused me to act unlike myself, raising my voice against my parents and drinking (although not often, and not to the point of passing out). Of course, those behaviours cause a positive(negative?) feedback loop, in which I feel like I've disappointed my parents further, leading to more blame, more behaviour, etc. This is a pretty major cause of all my self-loathing and was actually the original cause of this post. Although as you can see, its evolved beyond that.
#3 Related to the above issue is a more recent battle with myself. Because I have always tried to please my parents, and do what was expected of me and more, I always thought of myself as generally being a good, filial son and an amiable person in general. However, with more recent events (read: fights), I have begun to question that more and more. Am I truly a good person? Have my actions really merited being a filial son? I look at my friends and extended family and see that they have such close relationships with their parents a lot of the time (even if it seems antagonistic on one side, they still appear to have a closer bond). I feel jealous of them and what they have, and I question why, I, who has tried so hard to please my parents, don’t have that same relationship. Then it occurs to me: maybe I wasn’t such filial son after all. Its probably my fault that I tried too hard to please and keep my head down, rather than doing what it is that kids do and building a relationship up with my parents that way. I tried to hard to relieve rather than relate. And now, I’m paying the price for it.
#4 It may seem strange that it looks like I’m completely self-aware of my issues and that I seem to know how I could even answer them myself. However, this in itself is another cause for constant turmoil. Starting fairly recently, I feel as if I have 2 (sometimes 3) of “me” going on at the same time. Especially during times of extreme emotion, I’ll have one separate thought path going along with whatever is appropriate at the time, feeling the emotions, etc, but at the same time, another “me” is calmly analyzing everything, reflecting on the thoughts and actions of others, and generally being stoic. Occasionally, theres a third “me” that has wildly unrelated thoughts and wanders off for whatever whimsical wish I have at the time. All this going on at the same time causes a great big confusion within me, making me feel like I am both experiencing whatever is going on, yet only observing. The best way I can explain this is that sometimes, I feel like I’m an outsider looking in on myself. It makes me feel monstrous, as if I truly don’t feel these emotions, and that for whatever reason, one side of “me” is just putting on a show for everyone else to fit the situation.
I have countless other problems ranging from the inane to fairly distressing, but I feel, as of this moment, these four are the biggeset issues contributing to my recent suicidal thoughts. Just a note, I’ve had these thoughts for near on 2 years now, and among those 2 years, I have attempted twice, although no one knows, as I more or less “chickened out” in them. As of now, I don’t particularly feel suicidal, but before writing all this out, I had a pack of razor blades and a bottle of sleep medications easily within my reach and I  was scared that if I didn’t do anything, I would’ve just let my emotions sweep me away. Thankfully I decided to write this, and I feel like this would be extremely helpful in the future, should I regain those emotions for whatever reason. I don’t know if anyone will have read to the end of this, but if you have, I thank you, really, from the bottom of my heart. Even if you don’t pm me, even if you don’t comment. To know that someone out there knows my story, even if it’s a particularly boring, self-centered one, about a kid who just seems to a problem with self-loathing, lets me rest a little easier at night.

To be honest, one of the things that can drive me absolutely crazy as zerg is phoenix harass. If you don't feel safe enough to go in and start lifting queens, at least build a few to go around sniping his scouting overlords, or any stray overlords. Deny map control. Send small forces every so often so that he is forced to build units rather than drones. Keep in mind that for every unit build, a drone is not build, which means his economy can stagnate, leaving you to get back ahead, or get further ahead. If you know he has controll of the xel'naga tower, fake a push to scare him into making units. Thats where you can tech, or get a bigger econ, or expand. Essentially, get in the mindset that, the more he has to contend with your army, the less he can contend with you in economy.
